transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-05-15
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Acme Head of ML), Tess Alvarez (Acme CTO), Mateo Ruiz (Acme Procurement)

Summary (auto-generated): Quick renewal + expansion checkin. Customer wants more capacity and a new region. Follow ups on pricing and security docs.

[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, i think we have about 45 minutes, quick agenda — renewal numbers, capacity upgrades, region add, then any procurement questions. jordan / tess — are you on my side?
[00:16] Jordan (Acme): yep, hi alex, thanks. we have a few folks dialed in, just to confirm current usage, we're hitting our committed throughput during peak and the app is borderline on latency, we want to avoid tail latency spikes.
[00:30] Priya (Redwood SE): thanks jordan. a couple of data points from our end — your current Dedicated pool is about 70% utilized during peak windows; average token latency is within SLA but we are seeing variance when batch sizes hit 8-12.
[00:45] Tess (Acme): that aligns with what product is seeing, sometimes customers complain about thier realtime flows. We're exploring adding another region (eu-west-1) to reduce latency for EMEA and also want to bump reserved capacity for holiday season.
[01:05] Alex: got it. so two asks: additional region + capacity bump. for capacity are you thinking of doubling, or a smaller increment?
[01:15] Jordan: ideally double for throughput headroom, but cost is a factor. if we can get predictable pricing for 6-12 months that helps justify it.
[01:28] Mateo (Procurement): timeline wise, procurement wants a contract extension with updated committed units and a clear pricing table. we need final terms by end of may to get approval for june spend.
[01:40] Priya: on the technical side, adding eu-west-1 is straightforward but we need to run a short benchmark to validate model variants and kernel selection. we should replicate peak workflows — batching, prefixes, kv cache behavior.
[01:58] Jordan: yes please. we also have compliance questions — we need to ensure keys don't leave our KMS and audit logs are retained for 1 year.
[02:12] Alex: we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and we can integrate with your KMS for Dedicated through our key wrapping patterns, i'll share the SOC2 and KMS integration docs after the call.
[02:26] Tess: and what about fallbacks? if capacity hits the limit, can we route to hosted or lower-cost regions? we need graceful degradation.
[02:38] Priya: yes, smart routing can be configured — policy-based routing by latency or cost with automatic fallback to hosted. there's a small config window to adjust model variants to keep response quality.
[02:52] Jordan: how much lead time for provisioning another Dedicated pool in eu-west-1?
[03:00] Alex: from commit to ready typically 2-3 weeks for Dedicated, could be faster if we pre-allocate; pricing differs for multi-region. If you need 2x capacity in both regions that moves the pricing tier.
[03:15] Mateo: on pricing — any flexibility for a multi-quarter commit? we can do 12 months if there's a discount.
[03:24] Alex: yes we can do term discounts — i'll put together a shipment table with tiered pricing for 6 vs 12 months and include multi-region discounts.
[03:35] Priya: technical note — for benchmarking we'll need a small dataset of production prompts and a test harness; we can run both the current model variant and a quantized variant to compare latency/cost.
[03:50] Jordan: we'll provide prompts but some are sensitive. can we run the benchmark in customer VPC or will test data leave Acme?
[04:00] Priya: we can run the benchmark in a Private deployment or a VPC-connected Dedicated environment so data stays in your network. if that's not possible we can mask PII in the prompt set.
[04:12] Tess: procurement also needs to see proof of uptime — can you share SLA and recent incident history?
[04:20] Alex: yes i'll include the SLA doc and a short uptime summary. SOC2 report and security questionnaire will be attached.
[04:30] Mate o (Procurement): (laughs) thanks, i am mateo, just to clarify approval flow: we need legal and finance sign off, likely 2 weeks after we receive final quote.
[04:45] Alex: noted. we'll aim to get the quote to you by 2025-05-20 which leaves time for sign-off.
[04:52] Priya: is there any risk of compatibility with your model variants? we support standard open models and some optimizations may change output tone.
[05:05] Jordan: we have a quality bar — if quantization drops quality we'll stick with full precision for critical flows, maybe quantize for low-risk paths.
[05:18] Alex: good call. our Optimize team can provide model/quantization recommendations per route. i'll include the recommendations link.
[05:30] Tess: can you also include cost per 1M tokens with expected latency bands? Procurement wants that format.
[05:40] Alex: yes, pricing table will include per-token rates, reserved commit discounts, and estimated latency ranges per model/region.
[05:48] Jordan: fine. one more question — competitor angle: we're also evaluating Anthropic and Vertex for multi-region but your detailed latency benchmarks and model fidelity are big pluses.
[06:00] Alex: understood. we'll make sure the benchmark covers the comparison points you care about.
[06:10] (crosstalk)
[06:20] Mateo: and for procurement, please include who the Redwood contract owner is and invoicing details.
[06:28] Alex: will do.
[06:35] Priya: next steps recap — Alex sends updated quote and compliance package by 5/20; Priya schedules benchmark in eu-west-1 week of 5/26; Mateo confirms PO timeline by 5/22; Jordan shares a masked prompt set by 5/23.
[06:55] Tess: that works. thanks everyone.
[07:00] Alex: thanks all, we'll follow up via email and update the CRM.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcription has occasional mis-hearings (Mateo name captured as Mate o earlier). References: SOC2 report link (sent post-call), Draft quote (to be attached), Benchmark harness (link to runbook).
